name: ballerburg
why: A classic artillery duel with wind and terrain physics, an old-school game few developers have ever played.

brief.what_it_is: Ballerburg SDL is a classic two-player castle combat game for GNU/Linux and other systems supported by the SDL library. Two castles sit on either side of a mountain and fire cannonballs at each other, and a player wins by killing the opponent's king or by weakening the opponent until the king capitulates. The player builds up the castle with money, shaft towers and similar, as the opening quote from the king suggests. The fetched pages do not mention wind, although the scout notes describe wind and terrain physics, so treat that detail as unverified.
brief.why_it_exists: It is a port of Eckhard Kruse's 1987 Atari ST game Ballerburg to modern operating systems. The project page says Kruse released the original source code, which made the adaptation possible.
brief.install_notes: No binaries are provided. The homepage says: "Currently we provide only the source code of Ballerburg SDL, so please grab a source code tarball from our releases page and compile it on your own." The development version can be fetched with git clone https://framagit.org/baller/ballerburg.git. Pre-compiled packages for Fedora, Debian and Ubuntu are linked from the homepage, but I did not open those links. The game needs the SDL library installed. The brew formula's executable is named ballerburg. I did not find a README with build steps, so the exact build commands are unknown.
brief.standout: It is a faithful, open-source port of a 1987 Atari ST game, with the original code released by its author. Its three clone and remake cousins (a Ruby version, an X11-Basic version and a Mac OS X version) are linked from the homepage, which shows how long the design has been reimplemented.
brief.status: Unknown. The GitLab page shows the repository was created on February 12, 2025, but I saw no release date, last commit date, or version number. The homepage points to a releases page that I did not open.
brief.caveats: Source-only: you have to compile it yourself unless you use a distro package. It depends on SDL, so it runs only where SDL is supported. The license is GPLv3. The fetched pages do not describe the wind physics mentioned in the scout notes. The homepage and repo describe the game briefly, and I found no install or usage documentation beyond the homepage text.
quotes: Two castles, separated by a mountain, try to defeat each other with their cannonballs.
